newsitem.title: USA: U.S. farm trade surplus $1.393 billion in September.
newsitem.headline: U.S. farm trade surplus $1.393 billion in September.

text.p: The U.S. trade surplus in agricultural commodities was $1.393 billion in September, down from a revised $1.673 billion in August, the Commerce Department said Wednesday.

In its monthly trade report, Commerce pegged farm exports at $4.377 billion in September, down from the revised $4.709 billion in August. Imports were $2.984 billion, down from $3.036 billion the previous month.
The cumulative surplus in farm trade was $15.162 billion in January to September, compared with $12.189 billion in the same period last year.

In September, the value of U.S. wheat, corn and soybean exports all fell from the previous month. Wheat exports fell to $676 million from $797 million. Corn exports fell to $472 million from $568 million in August, and soybean exports fell to $542 million from $698 million, the department said.
Exports of meat and poultry were $540 million, down from $580 million in August.
Exports of fruits and frozen juice, wine, rice, nuts and oilseeds and food oils all rose.
